history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Jain (Digambara) Atishaya Kshetra, keep-or-drop decision needed. An 'atishaya kshetra' is a Jain pilgrimage site where buried idols were miraculously found. Lunwa has two Jain temples. The Khandelwal Digambar Jain Mandir (mulnayak Adinath) traces its founding to a Chandraprabha idol unearthed during digging near the Naraina village border; legend says a bullock cart carrying the disputed idol stopped on its own at Lunwa's Adinath temple ~45 km away, settling ownership. The second temple, Neminath Swami (Nasiya Ji) at the Lunwa bus stand, enshrines Chandraprabha and Shantinath idols reportedly found ~75 years ago while digging a well. Buried idols around the kshetra are claimed to date to the 6th century BCE (unverified, flag). CSV town 'Nagaur' corrected to Lunwa village; district corrected from Nagaur to Didwana-Kuchaman (post-2023 reorganisation).

name: Atishaya Kshetra Lunwa Jain Temple
town_description: Lunwa (Loonwa) is a small village near Nawa in Didwana-Kuchaman district, Rajasthan, about 70 km from Jaipur; the village is known principally as a Jain pilgrimage centre with two old Jain temples.

travel.road: Road from Jaipur (~70 km) via Nawa; village bus stand is next to the Neminath (Nasiya Ji) temple

visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 5:30 AM - 11:30 AM; evening from 6:00 PM (evening closing time not published, verify)
